summary: Full verification of the paste-anything UX overhaul (Steps 1/2/3) — backend + frontend. Backend: /app/backend/tests/test_paste_anything_flow.py (7 pytest cases, 5 classes) executed against preview URL. All 7 passed in 201.95s. Every acceptance criterion from the review is satisfied: (1) POST /api/projects/{id}/situation with {raw_paste} returns 200, Haiku extraction fills what/who/unclear, situation_input persists BOTH raw_paste and non-empty extracted fields; (2) same behaviour verified for /context (requirements/constraints/inspirations) and /decision (optimizing_for/tradeoffs/risks); (3) Backwards-compat legacy structured payloads (no raw_paste) still return 200 for both situation and context and persist fields as-is with NO raw_paste key; (4) Step 4 artifacts still generates scope_doc + client_message end-to-end when Steps 1-3 were completed via raw_paste; (5) Step 5 lock endpoint sets status='locked' and populates locked_at. Frontend: Playwright drove guest login → new project → Step 1: confirmed step1-paste-input exists (rows=12), label 'PASTE ANYTHING FROM YOUR CLIENT', helper mentions Email/WhatsApp/notes/Loom, and old testids step1-what-input / step1-who-input / step1-unclear-input / step1-what-suggest are ALL GONE. Short paste 'asdf' surfaces step1-paste-warning with the inline 'load a sample brief' link (step1-inline-sample-btn) and submit stays disabled. Filling 55 words reveals step1-word-count ('55 words · Bracket will extract what, who, and what's unclear.') and submit enables. step1-try-sample-btn pre-fills raw_paste (844 chars, realistic messy meeting-notes format) AND auto-submits; step1-framing-output appeared with reframed_problem + clarity label 'MURKY · 35'. Step 2: step2-paste-input rows=12, label 'PASTE ANYTHING ABOUT THIS PROJECT', helper mentions 'Requirements, constraints, references'; step2-word-count pill visible ('36 words · Bracket will extract requirements, constraints, and inspirations.'); old step2-req/con/insp all GONE; submitting a mixed paste produced step2-context-output within ~15s. Step 3: step3-paste-input rows=12, label 'PASTE YOUR THINKING ON THIS DECISION'; step3-word-count pill visible; old step3-opt/tr/rs all GONE; submitting produces the decision output with 'Rationale' and 'Alternatives' progressive-disclosure reveals visible in DOM. No console errors triggered by the paste flow.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L1328-1337 / L1370-1378 / L1408-1416: When raw_paste is provided, Haiku extraction runs and its output overwrites the structured fields, but the OR-fallback (`extracted['what'] or payload.get('what','')`) means if extraction returns an EMPTY string for a field while the same payload also carried a non-empty structured 'what', the legacy value silently wins. That's a fine safety net, but the review says 'extracted fields WIN over any structured fields also passed in the same payload' — the current code contradicts that when extraction is empty. Cheap fix: unconditionally overwrite once extraction succeeds. Not a bug per se, but the contract is ambiguous.

ai_engine.py extract_*_from_paste: on extraction failure the fallback stuffs the ENTIRE (up-to-2000 char) paste into the FIRST structured field (what / requirements / optimizing_for). The Sonnet prompt then embeds that full raw paste inline in a labelled 'What is the project:' line, which produces a slightly noisy prompt. Consider trimming to ~500 chars in the fallback, matching the normal cap, or wording the fallback content differently (e.g. prefix 'RAW_PASTE_FALLBACK: ...') so it doesn't masquerade as a clean extracted answer.

ProjectFlow.jsx L487-488 (Step 1) requires raw_paste.trim().length >= 20 AND !pasteGibberish; L819 (Step 2) requires >= 20 chars; L991 (Step 3) requires >= 15 chars. The 15-char threshold on Step 3 is inconsistent with Steps 1 & 2 (20) — probably intentional since Step 3 accepts terser stance statements, but worth documenting in a comment so a future refactor doesn't 'normalise' it.

server.py: no rate-limit / debounce on the extraction Haiku call. Because every submit fires an extra Haiku round-trip plus a Sonnet call, a user who mashes Reframe/Compress/Decide N times pays 2x LLM cost per press. Consider (a) caching extracted fields per raw_paste hash for the lifetime of a single project doc, or (b) exposing a client-side 'this paste hasn't changed since last call' guard so re-runs skip the extraction step.

SituationIn / ContextIn / DecisionIn (models.py): raw_paste is Optional[str] with no max_length. Coupled with the 8000-char slice in ai_engine.py, this is safe against blowup but the API contract should still declare a Field(max_length=20000) so Pydantic rejects megabyte pastes at the boundary instead of quietly truncating inside the LLM prompt.

server.py step_situation/step_context/step_decision: on Haiku extraction failure (network blip, JSON parse error), the fallback still triggers the Sonnet main call. That's the right choice UX-wise, but there's no observability hook — consider incrementing a Prometheus/log counter for `bracket.extraction.fallback` so ops can see when extraction is silently failing.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — every UI acceptance criterion from the review confirmed via Playwright

test_credentials: Guest session via POST /api/auth/guest (no credentials). Preview URL: https://design-decided.preview.emergentagent.com
seed_data_creation: Per-test-run projects named 'TEST_paste_{ts}', 'TEST_legacy_{ts}', 'TEST_ctx_legacy_{ts}', 'TEST_flow_{ts}' created under fresh guest sessions. A module-scoped autouse teardown deletes every TEST_* project via DELETE /api/projects/{id} before the session ends. The guest users themselves are ephemeral (synthetic guest-NN@use-bracket.com emails) and don't need explicit cleanup — they were also covered by iteration 23's admin purge if needed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Paste-anything path is production-ready: POST /api/projects/{id}/situation|/context|/decision now accept {"raw_paste": "..."} and store BOTH the raw_paste AND Haiku-extracted structured fields. Legacy structured payloads (no raw_paste) still work identically to before. Frontend testids to reference: Step 1 → step1-paste-input, step1-word-count, step1-paste-warning, step1-inline-sample-btn, step1-try-sample-btn, step1-submit-btn, step1-framing-output, step1-continue-btn. Step 2 → step2-paste-input, step2-word-count, step2-submit-btn, step2-context-output, step2-continue-btn, step2-back-btn. Step 3 → step3-paste-input, step3-word-count, step3-submit-btn, step3-continue-btn, step3-back-btn. Sample brief button is step1-try-sample-btn (pre-fills AND auto-submits). Old testids step1-what-input/step1-who-input/step1-unclear-input/step1-what-suggest/step2-req/step2-con/step2-insp/step3-opt/step3-tr/step3-rs have been REMOVED — do not reference them. Full-step timing: expect ~15-25s per step (Haiku extraction 1-3s + Sonnet main call 10-20s). Fresh guest sessions have zero projects on dashboard, so any regression test that needs a completed project must go through Steps 1-3 first (each step advances project.step so navigating to /projects/{id}/step/N is gated on prior step completion). Step 4/5 UI code path is untouched by this refactor — backend regression proved end-to-end works when Steps 1-3 came from raw_paste.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — new-feature verification. Zero bugs found in behaviour. Six code-review comments documented above are hardening suggestions (extraction-empty-wins ambiguity, fallback prompt noise, Step 3 char-threshold inconsistency, no de-duplication on repeated presses, missing Pydantic max_length on raw_paste, no observability counter on extraction fallback) — none block release.
